question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u$ and $w$ are orthogonal. Find $(u-2v)\cdot w+u\cdot (v+2w).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $w$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot w=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u-2v)\cdot w+u\cdot (v+2w) & =u\cdot w-(2v)\cdot w+u\cdot v+u\cdot (2w) \\  & =u\cdot w-2(v\cdot w)+u\cdot v+2(u\cdot w) \\  & =0-2(v\cdot w)+u\cdot v+0 \\  & =-2(v\cdot w)+u\cdot v \\  & =-2(2\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 1) \\  & +(2\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+3\cdot (-2)+5\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-2(-4+0+0-1)+(4+0-6-5) \\  & =10-7 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
